title: Hinduja Global Solutions Ltd - 532859 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HGS Q1 FY27 revenue flat at Rs 1,050.4 crore (-0.6% YoY) while EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% from 15.7% QoQ, with a PAT loss of Rs 66.3 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 1,050.4 crore, down 3.2% QoQ and 0.6% YoY, as a large client engagement is being phased out. EBITDA fell to Rs 116.3 crore (9.7% margin) from 15.7% in Q4, which management attributed to one-time phase-out costs, ramp and training costs on new wins, and front-loaded investment in sales, domain hiring and AI (Agent X). Net loss was Rs 66.3 crore against a Rs 13.6 crore loss in the previous quarter. Management said the new business carries more technology content and outcome-linked pricing, with margin benefits expected ahead of revenue growth in later quarters.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs +14.1 crore QoQ; Rs -26.5 crore YoY
vs Rs -13.6 crore QoQ; Rs +11.2 crore YoY (prior year incl. Rs 57.5 crore discontinued ops)
vs Rs 48.1 crore QoQ; Rs 57.9 crore YoY
vs Rs 5,346 crore at March 2026; borrowings Rs 1,279 crore

segments.name: CX services
segments.commentary: 54% of Q1 operating revenue. Vertical mix shows Tech, Media and Telecom at 46% of total revenue, with CG and Retail 19%, BFSI 17%, Public Sector 12%, Health and Life Sciences 3%, others 4%.

segments.name: Digital and Media services
segments.commentary: 46% of Q1 operating revenue. Broadband (ONEOTT/CelerityX) growing; high-speed (above 100 Mbps) share of subscribers rose to 15% from 11% a year ago. Digital television (linear TV) faces structural headwinds, mitigated via broadband bundling, IPTV and cost optimisation.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth and margins to pick up before the end of FY27, as the planned ramp-downs conclude within the current fiscal year.
Management views the Q1 margin hit as one-time investment absorption, not a structural change in earning power, and expects operating leverage to return as volume normalises.
Management expects AI and platform services to be medium-term margin accretive rather than dilutive.
Management is cautiously optimistic; macro uncertainty and client prudence may persist near term, with gradual improvement in growth and margins expected through the year.
Project Ganga is expected to enter operational mode in Q2 FY27; management said reporting will be in a different position at end of Q2.
Management expects the largest growth driver in FY27 to be AI and digital, with existing clients as the main source of growth.
capex_capacity: Project Ganga (launched 9 June 2026 in Uttar Pradesh) targets enabling 8,000 to 10,000 Nyaya Panchayat entrepreneurs as digital service providers, 50% women, and connecting over 2 million households over 2 to 3 years; about 2,000 applications and about 500 applicants trained as of 4 August 2026.

Project Ganga is funded primarily through internal accruals; management said it is run on a no-profit, no-loss basis for the network rollout, with ISP pricing in line with competition in Uttar Pradesh.
New subsidiary HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC incorporated in Dubai to build technology and consulting capabilities in the MENA region.
Investments in domain hiring, fractional advisors, solutions build-out, Agent X and the 90-day proof-of-value model were front-loaded in Q1.
demand_pricing: Added 19 new logos across CX and digital services and 8 clients in HRO and payroll processing in Q1; approximately 78 to 79 new logos were added in FY26.
New engagements start at about $150,000 to $300,000 in annual work and take 6 to 8 months to reach meaningful scale; initial 3 months carry training and ramp-up costs.
New AI-linked deals are smaller in revenue size but carry higher margins; AI share of work in new deals is expected to scale from 20-30% to 60-70%.
Pricing is shifting toward outcome-linked and non-headcount commercial structures; clients are moving from AI pilots to production but many are not yet ready on data and governance.
Broadband: customers choosing higher base plans; 10-30 Mbps entry plan share fell to 18% from 22%; 31-100 Mbps stable at about 67%.
Lost contracts were largely labour-priced; new contracts carry technology content and offshore-weighted delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Ankit Jain asked what margins HGS expects on Project Ganga, and whether it is subsidised.
qa_highlights.answer: Vynsley Fernandes said HGS acts as enabler and knowledge partner; pricing is in line with Uttar Pradesh competition, the no-profit-no-loss framing relates to supporting network rollout, and it is not a negative cash flow play.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked how quickly the new logos will contribute to revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh Korla said benefits typically take 6 to 8 months, with margin pressure in the first months; he expects growth and margin-attractive revenue before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked what limits faster revenue growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combination of ramp-up time and planned ramp-downs of legacy contracts, which should conclude before FY27 ends; new deals are smaller in revenue size but higher margin.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked whether clients are moving from Agentic AI pilots to production.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said demand for production deployments is strong but many customers lack data and governance readiness; he expects deployments to grow larger through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked where HGS has a sustainable AI edge as foundation models commoditise.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said the edge lies in applying models to industry-specific process re-engineering, which benefits HGS as model costs fall.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked how to measure Agent X success over 12 to 18 months.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will track number of customers and contracts with AI embedded and may look at measuring the share of revenue influenced by AI.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked whether the intelligent experiences positioning is producing larger, multi-towered deals.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said every recent new deal has AI components and that deals are becoming multi-towered, which he expects to lift revenue and margins over time.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on new engagements ramping: management guided that the 6 to 8 month ramp and 3-month training costs will weigh on margins before revenue growth shows up.
Legacy contract ramp-downs continue until the end of FY27; revenue growth is contingent on these concluding as planned and new deals being smaller in revenue size.
Digital television (linear TV) faces structural headwinds; management said the challenge remains on DTV and relies on bundling, IPTV and cost optimisation for mitigation.

Project Ganga economics: pricing is in line with Uttar Pradesh competition and framed as no-profit, no-loss for network rollout; Q2 FY27 operational start and promised KPIs (trained, loans under CM YUVA scheme, networks rolled out, customers onboarded) are next checkpoints.

Agent X and AI revenue attribution: management has not yet defined a revenue metric and said it would take away the question on measuring AI-influenced revenue; clients' data and governance readiness may slow production deployments.
key_quotes: The impact on margins is immediate because of ramp and training costs.
Consistent with what we have said in our prior quarters, we view this as a one-time cost and investment phase absorption, rather than any structural change in our earning power.
Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic, macro uncertainties and client prudence may persist in the near term and our 1st Quarter reflects that
Before the end of the year, we should start seeing growth and being margin-attractive to the company.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management framed the Q1 margin drop (EBITDA 9.7%) as one-time phase-out, ramp and investment costs and repeatedly guided to recovery before FY27 ends. It was less specific on near-term growth, citing macro uncertainty and client prudence, and it did not give quantified FY27 targets.

adds.what: Project Ganga digital service network: 8,000-10,000 Nyaya Panchayat entrepreneurs, 2 million households over 2-3 years (Uttar Pradesh)

growth.why: Revenue fell 3.2% QoQ and 0.6% YoY on legacy client phase-outs; management expects growth and margin pick-up before FY27 end, but gives only directional guidance with no numeric revenue target, and Project Ganga is funded from internal accruals on a no-profit, no-loss basis.
